newsitem.title: VIETNAM: U.S. senators urge Vietnam to uphold press freedom.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators urge Vietnam to uphold press freedom.

text.p: Visiting U.S. senators said on Tuesday they were concerned about press freedoms in Vietnam following Hanoi's refusal last month to renew a visa for a resident American journalist.
Democrat senator Thomas Daschle told a news conference in Hanoi that he and other members of the delegation had discussed a range of issues including human rights with senior Vietnamese officials.

Asked about Hanoi's recent decision to refuse a visa renewal for U.S. journalist Adam Schwarz he said: "We are deeply concerned about journalists not having the opportunity to do their work here in a full and open way."
"Certainly we want to impress upon the Vietnamese government our strong desire to ensure the freedom and the independence of journalism, as it is commonly known here in this country."
Daschle did not elaborate on his remarks or clarify whether the issue had been raised directly in the talks with Vietnamese officials including Communist Party chief Do Muoi.
Schwarz, a correspondent for the Hong Kong-based Far Eastern Economic Review magazine, left Vietnam on November 1.
His departure marked the first time a foreign journalist had been officially compelled to leave since overseas news organisations were allowed to set up bureaux in Hanoi more than six years ago.
Vietnam gave no reason for the move. A foreign ministry statement described it as "a normal thing".
